explanation.text: CPIAUCSL is defined as a price index of a basket of consumer goods and services paid by urban consumers, with components including food, shelter, fuels, transportation, service fees, and sales taxes, and price changes are averaged with weights representing their importance in consumer spending.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is described as a measure of average price change for a representative basket of consumer goods and services, with weights summing to 100 and composition including food, clothing, shelter, fuels, transportation fares, service fees, and sales taxes.

The CPI tracks price changes for consumer goods and services as a measure of inflation, with regular national publication beginning in 1921 and indexes estimated back to 1913, collected periodically from housing units and retail establishments across urban areas.

excerpts.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items (CPIAUCSL) is a price index of a basket of goods and services paid by urban consumers.

The CPIs are based on prices for food, clothing, shelter, and fuels; transportation fares; service fees (e.g., water and sewer service); and sales taxes. Prices are collected monthly from about 4,000 housing units and approximately 26,000 retail establishments across 87 urban areas. To calculate the index, price changes are averaged with weights representing their importance in the spending of the particular group. The index measures price changes (as a percent change) from a predetermined reference date.
